spec.description: Borges' map of the Empire the size of the Empire, in five tabs: four USGS sheets around Rhyolite, Nevada, from 1:250,000 (1908) to 1:24,000 (1987), each a quarter of the one before, and the last laid at 1:1 over the town and torn by the years while the animals recorded there move into its ruins.

options.content:
| | |
|---|---|
| Maps | The [USGS Historical Topographic Map Collection](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/national-geospatial-program/historical-topographic-maps-preserving-past) (public domain): Furnace Creek at 1:250,000 (1908), Bullfrog at 1:125,000 (1942), Bullfrog at 1:62,500 (1954) and Beatty at 1:24,000 (1987), the USGS's georeferenced GeoTIFF scans |
| Placing | Each sheet clipped at its neatline and moved from NAD27 to WGS 84 with NOAA's grids, in Web Mercator. A scan's own georeferencing can be off by a few tens of metres |
| The 1:1 map | The 1987 sheet over the town of Rhyolite at 2.5 m a pixel, 2.85 by 2.22 km, in eight stages of five years from 1987: torn along a fractal field (seeded 1946, the year of the story) and bleached toward the sand. Drawn, not observed |
| Animals | [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org) occurrences of animals in the town with coordinates and a year, under CC0 or CC BY 4.0 (CC BY-NC records left out): 537 records of 76 kinds, from 1913 to 2026, named after the GBIF backbone. Each record's dataset is in its tooltip |
| Rhyolite | The magenta ring on every map: Rhyolite where the USGS's [Geographic Names Information System](https://www.usgs.gov/tools/geographic-names-information-system-gnis) puts it (feature 845627), 36.90384° N, 116.82924° W |
| Satellite | The satellite base map, credited on the map |
| The story | Jorge Luis Borges, *Del rigor en la ciencia* (On Exactitude in Science), 1946 |
| Built by | `datasets/borges/build.sh` in [pacha-dashboards](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/pacha-dashboards) |

options.content:
**Furnace Creek, 1908.** One degree of desert across Nevada and California, with Death Valley along its western edge.

In 1908 Rhyolite, near the top of the sheet, was three years old: a gold town of a few thousand people, reached by three railways.

In Borges' story *On Exactitude in Science*, the cartographers of an Empire are never satisfied: the map of a province comes to fill a city, and the map of the Empire a province. These five tabs go down that ladder. Each map is a quarter of the one before, printed on about the same sheet of paper; the yellow frame is the next one.

spec.rawSql:
WITH w AS (SELECT least(2026, greatest(1987, year(coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'))))::INTEGER AS y)
SELECT count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Animals" FROM $animals, w WHERE year <= w.y

spec.description: GBIF occurrences of animals in the town (CC0 and CC BY 4.0) with a year up to the window's year.
spec.title: Animals recorded by then

spec.rawSql:
-- The years the brush is drawn over: the animals GBIF records in the town each year, and the paper left.
WITH years AS (SELECT unnest(generate_series(TIMESTAMP '1987-01-01', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01', INTERVAL 1 YEAR)) AS "time")
SELECT y."time",
       (SELECT count(*) FROM $animals a WHERE a.year = year(y."time"))::DOUBLE AS "Animals recorded",
       (SELECT 100 * s.paper_left FROM $stages s WHERE year(y."time") BETWEEN s.year_from AND s.year_to) AS "Paper left (%)"
FROM years AS y
ORDER BY y."time"

spec.description: Every view takes the first year of the window: drag it, step it or press play to run the years from 1987. Bars: animals recorded in the town each year; line: the share of the paper still there.
spec.title: Years since the map was laid: brush or play

spec.rawSql:
WITH w AS (SELECT least(2026, greatest(1987, year(coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'))))::INTEGER AS y)
SELECT count(DISTINCT animal)::DOUBLE AS "Kinds" FROM $animals, w WHERE year <= w.y

spec.description: Different species (or genera, when the species is unknown) among them.
spec.title: Kinds of animals

spec.rawSql:
-- The 1987 sheet over the town at 1:1, as torn as the brush's year leaves it: one file every five years.
WITH w AS (SELECT least(2026, greatest(1987, year(coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'))))::INTEGER AS y)
SELECT 'http://feeds/datasets/borges/' || file AS raster_url FROM $stages, w WHERE w.y BETWEEN year_from AND year_to

-- The animals GBIF holds for the town, recorded by the brush's year: they live in the ruins of the map.
WITH w AS (SELECT least(2026, greatest(1987, year(coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS TIMESTAMP), TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01'))))::INTEGER AS y)
SELECT latitude, longitude, coalesce(english, animal) AS name, animal AS scientific, CASE class WHEN 'Aves' THEN 'Aves' WHEN 'Squamata' THEN 'Squamata' WHEN 'Mammalia' THEN 'Mammalia' WHEN 'Insecta' THEN 'Insecta' ELSE 'Other' END AS "group",
       year, licence, dataset
FROM $animals, w WHERE year <= w.y

-- Rhyolite where the USGS's Geographic Names Information System puts it (feature 845627): the same mark on every map.
SELECT 36.90384 AS latitude, -116.82924 AS longitude, 'Rhyolite' AS label

The dots are the animals recorded in the town by then, coloured by group: birds blue, lizards and snakes red, mammals purple, insects green. spec.title: Rhyolite at 1:1: the paper in the desert

The map the size of the town

options.content:
**Rhyolite at 1:1.** The 1987 sheet, enlarged until it matches the ground point by point, laid over the town: a sheet of 2.85 by 2.22 km. The generations that followed, the story goes, found such a map useless and left it to the sun and the winters.

Press play: from 1987 the paper tears and bleaches, five years at a time, until a fifth of it is left. The animals recorded in the town move into its ruins: side-blotched lizards, ravens, rock wrens, zebra-tailed lizards.

> «Ruinas despedazadas del Mapa, habitadas por Animales y por Mendigos»
>
> Jorge Luis Borges, *Del rigor en la ciencia*, 1946

The tears are drawn, not observed. The animals are real records.

options.content:
**Beatty, 1987.** The most detailed sheet the USGS drew here: every mine, dump and gate. Rhyolite is a name, *Ruins* and an *Old RR Grade*.

One step remains. In the story, the Colleges of Cartographers build a map of the Empire the size of the Empire, which coincides with it point by point.
